subject: maths
question: Three pipes, P, Q and R, together take four hours to fill a tank. All the three pipes were opened at the same time. After three hours, P was closed, and Q and R filled the remaining tank in two hours. How many hours will P alone take to fill the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Part of the tank filled by P, Q and R in 3 hours = 3/4

Remaining part of the tank = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4

Q and R fill 1/4 part in 2 hours → they can fill the full tank in 8 hours.

Efficiency of P = Total efficiency − Efficiency of (Q + R) = (1/4) − (1/8) = 1/8

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (P + Q + R) to fill the tank together = 4 hours

Time taken by (Q + R) to fill the remaining tank after 3 hours = 2 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work completed by (P + Q + R) in 3 hours = 3/4

⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4

⇒ Time taken by (Q + R) to fill the complete tank = 2 × 4 = 8 hours

⇒ Efficiency of P = Efficiency of (P + Q + R) − Efficiency of (Q + R)

⇒ Efficiency of P = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Time taken by P alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of P

⇒ Time taken by P alone = 8 ÷ 1 = 8 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, the part of the tank filled by the pipe in 1 hour is 1/x.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

Fractional Work

If a/b part of a work is completed in T days, then the total work will be completed in T × (b/a) days.
